items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1969-12-04
items.q: So I signed up with Vincent Lopez. And he appointed Mrs. Marvin Fuller, Mrs. Earl Fuller as my manager.

ctx.x: But your New York recordings had a two-bone. They're too long you say? No, there's a tuba, tuba player.

I had a tuba player, Barney Aquilino. He was with James Barney. I got him afterwards in New York. And he was more or less my promoter. He got me in the middle of a dance hall. I wore up in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania. There was two dance halls, big ball, beautiful big ball. They were fighting each other. And I happened to play at the six day bicycle races. You see I lived a long life, and I'll tell you a long, I mean a musical life. I'm playing at the six day bicycle races for the benefit of poor children. And in…
She was in early movies, in silent movies?

items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: I signed up with Vincent Lopez's office... So Vincent Lopez sent me and I was coming home.

ctx.x: Well we have books that tell all about your records.

You see if I had been like, I was doing so well and I was so busy that I didn't have time to put dates on anything or who the person was. I played in the All-Star Orchestra in Chicago when I was at the Green Mill. I played at the Green Mill in Chicago for Tom Chimali. And I was this trumpet player selected to play with all the stars and I can't tell you who they were and I know they must be all famous musicians. I went there to some big ballroom, we sat down, they handed out the music, we played it. The piano…

Okay. How would you contrast the public taste in music, especially in New Orleans, as it changed during the years from the first that you remember to about 1930? What kind of music did people seem to want in those years, at various times?
